title: Succession of coast pine barrens to northern hardwoods in a lacustrine sand dune system
content:
by Grace W. Auckley, Jordan M. Marshall

The Grand Sable Dunes is a perched lacustrine dune system within Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore, USA, on Lake Superior. Wind provides disturbance which has continually influenced the successional pathways of these dunes. The objectives of this study were to identify the relationships between forest stand age, successional processes, and overall forest development by categorizing forest type and regeneration patterns, mapping the dendrochronological sequence, and quantifying coarse woody debris (CWD) accumulation in the Grand Sable Dunes. We surveyed the understory, midstory, and overstory woody vegetation across 43 plots. Cores from the four largest trees were collected and CWD volume was measured within each plot. Results indicated that there is a chronosequence across the dunes that is supported by forest type, stand age, and CWD. There was a positive relationship between distance from shore and midstory and overstory diversity, stand age, and CWD accumulation. The rows closest to Lake Superior were at an earlier successional stage and dominated by jack pine (Pinus banksiana) and sand cherry (Prunus pumila) with zero CWD and mean stand age less than 18 years. The southern rows (farthest from Lake Superior) were at a more advanced successional stage with sugar maple (Acer saccharum) as the dominant species with the greatest amount of CWD and mean stand age nearly 100 years. The mid-dune rows were at a transitional stage with mature jack pine and hardwood species establishing with greater variation in CWD and a mean stand age of 39 years. Overall, the Grand Sable Dunes appear to be following the traditional successional pattern and linear chronosequence across the dunes despite general debate over successional processes and the complexity of a chronosequence. These results will clarify future forest patterns, as well as structural and compositional changes occurring within lacustrine sand dune ecosystems.
